To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genome-wide gene expression in LPS stimulated macrophages is biphasic with i) a sharp acute response consisting of small number (few %) of highly induced immune-related genes followed by ii) a collective mode of weakly induced (few fold) genes of diverse cellular functions which collectively adjust their level to achieve a steady state.
the genome-wide response to LPS is biphasic and the transition from stochastic to collective mode is an emergent organizing principle.

i) genome-wide response to LPS is biphasic and ii) the transition from stochastic mode of acute response to collective mode of chronic response emerges as an organizing mechanism to decipher whole genome response to LPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the organizing principles that underlie the emergent whole genome control of gene expression.
the emergent properties of the whole genome responses in wildtype and genetically mutated LPS-stimulated macrophages.
the emergent behavior of whole genome response in wildtype and genetically mutated LPS stimulated macrophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the whole genome response to LPS is highly co-regulated and the emergent genome-wide control is a consequence of the concerted actions of multiple gene regulatory networks.
the emergent genome-wide control of gene expression is a fundamental property of the biological systems and it is not an artifact of the experimental design.
, in addition to a small number of sharply regulated immune-related genes, a large number of genes are weakly co-regulated in the collective mode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the emergent behavior of the entire gene expression network can be understood by studying a small number of genes.

the genome-wide response to LPS is biphasic; the acute-stochastic response is dominated by the action of MyD88 and TRIF, while the collective response is a result of the action of multiple regulatory processes.
a large number of genes are weakly induced in a coordinated manner to fine tune the expression levels of a small number genes which have a sharp induction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emergent genome-wide control is a fundamental property of the gene regulatory network and should not be ignored when analyzing large-scale gene expression data.
the emergent whole genome control is the result of collective action of the entire network of genes and their interactions.

the emergent behavior of gene expression in wildtype and genetically mutated LPS stimulated macrophages can be explained by the superposition of the role of Myd88, TRIF-dependent and independent processes.
